epics.title: E17 — Inventory & Equipment
epics.description:
## Outcome
Weapons, armor, books, keys, consumables, quest objects and unusual artifacts are manageable without inventory busywork. Equipment changes what the player can *do* (new verbs, altered stealth/noise, light, traversal), not only numbers. All rules live in `src/sim` with data in `src/content`.
## Scope
- In: Item definition schema + validator, inventory model, equip slots, keyring, consumables, pickup/drop/throw, equipment-granted verbs, inventory/equipment UI, save integration, debug commands
- In: Encumbrance decision via spike (weightless vs light encumbrance)
- Out: Loot tables and containers (mw-e18)
- Out: Spell learning from books (e07-spellbook-learning; we only model books as items)
- Out: Shops and prices (mw-e20)
- Out: Specific item content lists for Briar Glen (world-content group)
## Exit criteria
- Player can pick up, inspect, equip, use, drop and throw items in the greybox testbed with keyboard+mouse and gamepad.
- At least 3 equipment items grant a new verb or systemic property (e.g. light source, noise reduction, climb anchor) through the capability registry, verified by tests.
- Inventory and equipment round-trip through save/load with zero diffs across 100 randomized inventories.
- src/sim inventory/equipment modules and src/content item schema at 100% coverage.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Player can pick up, inspect, equip, use, drop and throw items in the greybox testbed with keyboard+mouse and gamepad.
- EC-2 At least 3 equipment items grant a new verb or systemic property (e.g. light source, noise reduction, climb anchor) through the capability registry, verified by tests.
- EC-3 Inventory and equipment round-trip through save/load with zero diffs across 100 randomized inventories.
- EC-4 src/sim inventory/equipment modules and src/content item schema at 100% coverage.

epics.title: E18 — Loot & Treasure
epics.description:
## Outcome
Exploration produces interesting, handcrafted discoveries rather than endless statistically interchangeable equipment. Loot is data (tables + placements), deterministic under seeded RNG, persistent in world state, and aware of ownership so theft is a real, systemic act.
## Scope
- In: Loot table schema + deterministic roller + validator, containers, placed/hidden treasure, creature drops, ownership + stolen flag, unique artifacts with verbs, container/loot UI, treasure design guide, loot audit tool
- Out: Random affix/stat-stick generation (explicitly rejected by the anti-grind rule)
- Out: Lockpicking and trap disarming mechanics (mw-e10) — containers only expose lock/trap hooks
- Out: Specific treasure placements for Briar Glen/Labyrinth (world-content group)
## Exit criteria
- A container in the greybox testbed can be opened, looted, and stays looted after save/reload.
- Taking an owned item while witnessed flags it stolen and emits a crime event consumed by AI; unwitnessed theft flags it stolen without a crime event.
- The loot validator rejects any table referencing a missing item, a duplicated unique, or a cyclic nested table.
- Roller is deterministic: same seed + same table yields identical results in 10,000-roll replay tests.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 A container in the greybox testbed can be opened, looted, and stays looted after save/reload.
- EC-2 Taking an owned item while witnessed flags it stolen and emits a crime event consumed by AI; unwitnessed theft flags it stolen without a crime event.
- EC-3 The loot validator rejects any table referencing a missing item, a duplicated unique, or a cyclic nested table.
- EC-4 Roller is deterministic: same seed + same table yields identical results in 10,000-roll replay tests.

epics.title: E19 — Progression
epics.description:
## Outcome
Character advancement primarily unlocks capabilities (verbs), specialization and new play styles — never Firebolt I → II (+12%). The player picks a class at the start; each class earns new verbs through its own fiction: books (sorcerer), techniques from trainers (knight), arrows and trick-shot techniques (archer), tools and tricks (thief). Supporting stats are minimal and subordinate.
## Scope
- In: Progression model ADR (incl. XP yes/no and respec policy), capability registry, progression core, class definitions as data, class selection, minimal supporting stats, per-class unlock channels, deed-based unlocks, capabilities screen + unlock feedback, respec implementation per ADR
- Out: Individual spells (mw-e08), spell learning mechanics (e07-spellbook-learning — we integrate with it)
- Out: Combat move implementation (mw-e04, mw-e05) and thief tool mechanics (mw-e10) — this epic only grants/gates the verbs
- Out: Specific trainer NPCs (world-content group)
## Exit criteria
- All four classes are defined purely in data and selectable at new game.
- Every class has at least one in-fiction unlock channel working end-to-end in grey-box (book, trainer, arrow schematic, tool).
- No progression data entry is a pure numeric increase of an existing capability unless flagged `supporting: true`; the content validator enforces this.
- Capabilities persist through save/load and are queryable by dialogue, quests, puzzles and interaction prompts.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 All four classes are defined purely in data and selectable at new game.
- EC-2 Every class has at least one in-fiction unlock channel working end-to-end in grey-box (book, trainer, arrow schematic, tool).
- EC-3 No progression data entry is a pure numeric increase of an existing capability unless flagged `supporting: true`; the content validator enforces this.
- EC-4 Capabilities persist through save/load and are queryable by dialogue, quests, puzzles and interaction prompts.

epics.title: E20 — Economy & Shops
epics.description:
## Outcome
Gold has meaningful uses and merchants have identities, inventories and specialties (Quest for Glory merchants with personality; Elder Scrolls living shops). Players can buy, sell, haggle and steal, and prices respond to disposition, specialty and stolen goods.
## Scope
- In: Economy design doc (income vs sinks), merchant schema + validator, pure price model, buy/sell transactions (anchor), restock/rotation, fences and stolen goods, shoplifting consequences, haggling, services as gold sinks, merchant barks, shop UI, economy balance tool
- Out: Bookshop-specific inventory rules (e21-bookshop-system builds on this epic)
- Out: Specific merchants and inventories for Briar Glen (world-content group)
- Out: Real-money anything (free game)
## Exit criteria
- A grey-box merchant supports buy, sell, haggle and theft with persistent stock and gold.
- Prices are a pure deterministic function of item value, merchant, disposition, specialty and stolen state, covered 100% by unit tests.
- Economy balance tool reports total obtainable gold vs total meaningful sinks for the MVP region and CI fails if ratio leaves the band set in the design doc.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 A grey-box merchant supports buy, sell, haggle and theft with persistent stock and gold.
- EC-2 Prices are a pure deterministic function of item value, merchant, disposition, specialty and stolen state, covered 100% by unit tests.
- EC-3 Economy balance tool reports total obtainable gold vs total meaningful sinks for the MVP region and CI fails if ratio leaves the band set in the design doc.

epics.title: E22 — NPC & Dialogue System
epics.description:
## Outcome
Characters support conversations with conditions and effects, disposition, meaningful choices, class-specific options, persuasion (Divinity: Original Sin 2 style), rumors that lead to places, and lightweight state tracking. Text only for MVP (no voice), with subtitle/text-size accessibility hooks. Dialogue is authored as validated data, never bespoke code.
## Scope
- In: Shared condition/effect DSL, dialogue authoring format + schema, dialogue runtime (anchor), disposition, class/capability-gated options, deterministic persuasion checks, rumors, gifts/bribes, NPC conversation hookup, dialogue UI with accessibility, ambient barks/subtitles, dialogue validator, preview/debug tooling
- Out: Specific Briar Glen NPCs and their dialogue (world-content group)
- Out: Social creature behaviours beyond dialogue (mw-e14)
- Out: Voice acting (not in MVP)
## Exit criteria
- A grey-box NPC conversation exercises conditions, effects, disposition changes, a class-gated option and a persuasion check end-to-end.
- Dialogue validator guarantees every node is reachable, every non-terminal node has an exit, and all references resolve; CI runs it on all dialogue content.
- Dialogue UI respects text-size, background opacity and reading-speed settings.
- Dialogue runtime and DSL at 100% coverage.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 A grey-box NPC conversation exercises conditions, effects, disposition changes, a class-gated option and a persuasion check end-to-end.
- EC-2 Dialogue validator guarantees every node is reachable, every non-terminal node has an exit, and all references resolve; CI runs it on all dialogue content.
- EC-3 Dialogue UI respects text-size, background opacity and reading-speed settings.
- EC-4 Dialogue runtime and DSL at 100% coverage.

epics.title: E23 — Quest Framework
epics.description:
## Outcome
Quests support branching objectives and multiple resolutions (including non-combat) authored as data without bespoke scripting. Quest state lives in the world-state store and persists; failure transitions continue the story instead of dead-ending it. Players track progress in an in-character journal.
## Scope
- In: Quest authoring format + schema, quest runtime (anchor), objective trackers bound to sim events, failure-continues-story transitions, quest validator (every quest resolvable), journal UI, optional wayfinding hints, debug/simulation tools, reference fixture quest, authoring guide
- Out: Specific Briar Glen quests and the main story (world-content / narrative groups, e39-story-bible)
- Out: Cutscene system (not planned for MVP)
## Exit criteria
- A reference grey-box quest can be resolved via at least three distinct resolutions (combat, stealth, dialogue) and a failure path, each covered by an automated e2e test.
- Quest validator proves every authored quest has at least one reachable resolution and every failure state has a continuation.
- Quest state round-trips through save/load mid-objective with no loss.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 A reference grey-box quest can be resolved via at least three distinct resolutions (combat, stealth, dialogue) and a failure path, each covered by an automated e2e test.
- EC-2 Quest validator proves every authored quest has at least one reachable resolution and every failure state has a continuation.
- EC-3 Quest state round-trips through save/load mid-objective with no loss.

items.title: Spike: decide encumbrance model (weightless vs light encumbrance)
items.description:
## Why
The epic outcome forbids inventory busywork, but some weight is useful when it creates decisions (heavy armor = loud and slow for stealth). We need a decision before the inventory model hardens.
## What
Time-box: 1 day. Question: which inventory capacity model best serves "no busywork" while keeping equipment choices meaningful? Evaluate (a) fully weightless with category tabs, (b) weightless inventory + equipped-armor weight that affects noise/stamina/movement verbs, (c) light encumbrance with generous soft cap, (d) grid/slot inventory. Also decide whether large world objects (crates, bodies, statues) are carried physically instead of stored.
## Scope
- In: Comparison matrix against constitution pillars, reference games (QfG5, DOS2, Skyrim, Zelda BotW)
- In: ADR in docs/adr/ with recommendation and consequences for mw-e17/mw-e10/mw-e09
- Out: Implementation (e17-inventory-core)
## Notes
Leaning: option (b) — inventory is weightless; only *equipped* armor/weapon weight class feeds e09 noise and stamina. Physically carried world objects handled by e03-physics-objects.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the spike is complete, when the ADR is reviewed, then docs/adr/ contains an encumbrance ADR with status "Accepted", the options matrix, and the chosen model.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it states explicitly how (if at all) equipment weight affects stealth noise, stamina and movement speed, with numeric ranges.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it lists the edge cases the model must handle: picking up an item while "full" (if caps exist), quest items, stacks, and physically carried world objects.

items.title: Define item definition schema and content validator
items.description:
## Why
Items are data, not code (contract §1). Every other systems epic (loot, shops, quests, progression) references item IDs, so a single validated schema is the foundation.
## What
A zod schema in src/content/items for item definitions: `id`, `category` (weapon, armor, shield, ammo, book, key, consumable, tool, quest, artifact, currency, misc), `nameKey`/`descKey` text ids, `icon` asset id, `value`, `stackable` + `maxStack`, `weightClass` (per encumbrance ADR), `worldProperties` (e03 tags so a dropped oil flask is flammable), `grants` (capability ids, see e19-capability-registry), `equip` (slot + class proficiency tags), `use` (effect list), `flags` (unique, questItem, noSell, noDrop).
## Scope
- In: Schema, TS types inferred from zod, loader integration, validator tests
- In: Cross-ref checks: icon asset ids exist in the asset manifest (placeholder allowed), capability ids exist, unique ids unique
- In: Five fixture items (one per major category) for tests
- Out: Inventory runtime (e17-inventory-core)
- Out: Actual game item content (world-content group)
## Notes
Keep `use` effects referencing the shared effect vocabulary from e22-condition-effect-dsl once it lands; until then a minimal effect union is acceptable and migrated later.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given a valid item fixture for each category, when validated, then validation passes and the inferred type exposes category-specific fields.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an item with `stackable: false` and `maxStack: 5`, when validated, then validation fails with a message naming the item id and field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two items with the same id, when the item catalogue is loaded, then loading fails listing both source files.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an item whose `grants` references an unknown capability id, when validated against the capability registry, then validation fails naming the capability.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an item flagged `questItem: true` without `noSell` and `noDrop`, when validated, then those flags are defaulted to true.

items.title: Implement inventory model with stacks, keys, books and quest items
items.description:
## Why
Players need to carry the things they discover without busywork; every loot, shop, quest and puzzle interaction reads or writes the inventory.
## What
As a player, I want picked-up items to land in a tidy inventory grouped by category so that I spend time adventuring, not sorting.

Pure sim module: `Inventory` holding item instances `{instanceId, defId, count, flags: {stolen?, ownerId?, bound?}}`. Operations: add (auto-stack; stolen and non-stolen never merge), remove, move-to-keyring/bookshelf views, query by category/tag/capability, gold as currency counter. Emits events (`item.added`, `item.removed`, `item.flagChanged`) on the sim event bus. Enforces capacity only as the encumbrance ADR dictates.
## Scope
- In: Inventory data structure, operations, events, category views (keys, books, quest objects, artifacts, consumables)
- In: Quest items cannot be removed except by effects with `force: true`
- In: Gold counter with overflow protection
- Out: Equip slots (e17-equipment-slots)
- Out: World pickup/drop (e17-world-pickup-drop)
- Out: Serialization (e17-inventory-persistence)
- Out: UI (e17-inventory-ui)
## Notes
Instances rather than bare counts so that stolen/owner flags and unique artifacts are tracked individually. Deterministic instance ids from the sim id generator (no Math.random).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an empty inventory, when 3 then 4 of a stackable item with maxStack 5 are added, then the inventory holds stacks of 5 and 2 and emits two `item.added` events.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an inventory holding 2 non-stolen apples, when 1 stolen apple is added, then there are two separate stacks and the stolen stack carries its ownerId.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a quest item in inventory, when a non-forced remove is requested, then removal is rejected with reason `quest-item` and the inventory is unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an inventory, when querying category `key`, then only key-category instances are returned in stable acquisition order.
- AC-5 [unit] Given gold at 2^31-10, when 100 gold is added, then gold clamps at the configured maximum and a `gold.capped` event is emitted.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a remove of more units than held, when executed, then it fails atomically and no partial removal occurs.

items.title: Add equipment slots with class proficiencies and equip events
items.description:
## Why
Weapons, shields, armor and tools must be equipped to matter; equip state drives combat, stealth noise and granted verbs.
## What
As a player, I want to equip weapons, armor and tools so that my character looks and plays differently.

Slots: mainHand, offHand, head, body, hands, feet, trinket×2, ammo (quiver), toolBelt×2. Two-handed items occupy both hands. Class proficiency is soft: non-proficient equips are allowed but apply a data-defined penalty (e.g. slower draw, louder) rather than an outright block, so improvisation is possible. Emits `equip.changed` events; exposes a derived `EquipmentState` (weight class, noise modifier, light emitted, granted capabilities list).
## Scope
- In: Slot model, equip/unequip/swap, two-handed rules, proficiency penalties from data, derived state, events
- Out: What granted capabilities do (e17-equipment-verbs)
- Out: Paper-doll UI (e17-equipment-ui)
- Out: Combat stats consumption (mw-e04/mw-e05)
## Notes
Derived noise/weight feed e09-visibility-model and e09-sound-propagation via the derived state; those epics consume it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sword in mainHand and a shield in offHand, when a two-handed greatsword is equipped, then both previous items return to inventory and both hand slots reference the greatsword.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sorcerer equipping heavy plate, when equipped, then the equip succeeds and the derived state includes the data-defined non-proficiency penalty.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an item without an `equip` block, when equip is requested, then it fails with reason `not-equippable`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given any equip change, when it completes, then exactly one `equip.changed` event is emitted with before/after slot maps.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the inventory ADR weight classes, when heavy body armor is equipped, then derived `weightClass` is `heavy` and `noiseModifier` matches the data value.

items.title: Auto-use keys from the keyring on matching locks
items.description:
## Why
Keys are core to exploration loops and shortcuts; fumbling through menus to use them is busywork.
## What
As a player, I want locked doors and chests to open automatically when I hold the right key so that finding the key is the reward.

Locks (e03-doors-locks-switches) expose `lockId`; keys declare `opens: [lockId]` or `opensTag`. Interacting with a lock checks the keyring; single-use keys are consumed; master keys open by tag. Missing key produces a contextual prompt hint ("Locked. Perhaps someone in town has the key.") driven by lock data.
## Scope
- In: Key matching, consumption rules, prompt text hooks, events for quests (`lock.opened` with keyId)
- Out: Lockpicking (mw-e10)
- Out: Forcing/smashing locks (mw-e03 / mw-e04)

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a door with lockId `tower-door` and a key whose `opens` includes it, when the player interacts, then the door unlocks and a `lock.opened` event records the key id.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a single-use key, when it opens its lock, then it is removed from the inventory; a reusable key remains.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lock with no matching key, when interacted with, then the lock stays locked and the prompt shows the lock's `lockedHintKey` text.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the greybox testbed door with a key placed nearby, when the player picks up the key and interacts with the door, then the door opens without opening any menu.

items.title: Use consumables from inventory and assignable quick slots
items.description:
## Why
Potions, food, oil flasks and scrolls are tactical tools; using them mid-fight must be fast and systemic.
## What
As a player, I want to drink, eat, apply or throw consumables from four quick slots so that I can react in combat without pausing.

Use pipeline: validate → apply `use` effects (heal, restore stamina/mana, apply status, coat weapon with oil, spawn thrown object) → consume one unit → emit `item.used`. Throwable consumables spawn a physics object carrying their world properties (a thrown oil flask shatters and leaves a flammable puddle via e03). Quick slots persist and auto-refill from same-def stacks; empty slots display as depleted.
## Scope
- In: Use pipeline, 4 quick slots, auto-refill, cooldown/animation-lock hook, throwables via world properties
- Out: Quick-slot HUD visuals (e17-inventory-ui)
- Out: Spell scrolls casting (e06-spell-pipeline consumes the effect)
## Notes
Effects expressed via property/effect vocabulary, never item-specific scripts (contract §5: properties, not pairings).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a healing draught in quick slot 1 and 3 in stock, when used, then health increases per data, stock becomes 2 and `item.used` is emitted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the last unit in a quick slot is used and another stack of the same def exists, when used, then the slot refills from that stack.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a throwable consumable with `worldProperties: [flammable, liquid]`, when thrown, then a spawn request is emitted carrying exactly those properties.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a consumable used while a use-lock is active, when the second use is requested, then it is rejected with reason `busy` and no unit is consumed.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox testbed, when the player throws an oil flask then ignites it, then the resulting area is on fire via e03 propagation (no flask-specific code).

items.title: Pick up, drop and throw items as physical world objects
items.description:
## Why
Items should exist in the world with properties (a dropped key can fall through a grate; a thrown bottle distracts a guard), reinforcing systemic play.
## What
As a player, I want to pick up items I see, and drop or throw items from my inventory so that I can use them as bait, distractions or puzzle pieces.

World item entity: mesh placeholder by category, interact prompt "Take <name>", pickup adds to inventory and removes entity; drop/throw spawns an entity with physics and world properties. Pickup respects ownership (owned items marked stolen via e18-ownership-stolen when it lands).
## Scope
- In: World item entity, pickup/drop/throw bindings, placeholder meshes per category, noise event on impact via e09 hook
- Out: Containers (e18-containers)
- Out: Ownership logic (e18-ownership-stolen)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an item entity within interact range, when the player interacts, then the item is added to inventory and the entity is despawned in the same sim tick.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an item in inventory, when dropped, then an item entity with identical instance flags (e.g. stolen) spawns in front of the player.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a thrown item that hits a surface, when impact resolves, then a noise event is emitted with loudness from the item weight class.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a quest item, when drop is requested, then it is rejected with reason `no-drop`.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the player picks up, drops and re-picks the same item, then inventory count returns to the original and no duplicate entity remains.

items.title: Serialize inventory, equipment and quick slots into saves
items.description:
## Why
The m1 loop ends with save/reload; losing or duplicating items breaks trust immediately.
## What
Register inventory, equipment and quick-slot state with the versioned save format. Includes migration stub, round-trip tests and property-based randomized inventories.
## Scope
- In: Save section schema, serialize/deserialize, migration v1 stub, round-trip + fuzz tests
- Out: World item entities in the level (owned by e27 world-state persistence)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 100 randomized inventories (seeded) with stolen flags, stacks and equipped items, when saved and loaded, then state is deep-equal to the original.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a save referencing an item def that no longer exists, when loaded, then the instance is dropped, a warning is logged, and the rest of the inventory loads.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a v1 inventory save, when the migration runner processes it at current version, then it loads without error.

items.title: Let equipment grant verbs and systemic properties
items.description:
## Why
Zelda-style meaningful items: equipment should unlock verbs (a lantern makes light, a grappling hook enables anchors, soft boots quiet footsteps), not just add stats.
## What
As a player, I want gear that changes what I can do so that finding a new item feels like finding a new ability.

Equipped items with `grants` register capabilities as source `equipment:<instanceId>` in the capability registry; unequipping revokes them. Items may also emit properties: `lightRadius` (feeds e03-light-field), `noiseModifier`, `carriesFire`, etc. Interaction prompts query capabilities so new options appear on world objects.
## Scope
- In: Grant/revoke on equip change, property emitters, prompt refresh event
- In: Three grey-box sample items: lantern (light), soft boots (noise), climbing hook (anchor verb)
- Out: The verbs' mechanics themselves (owned by their epics, e.g. climbing in mw-e10)
## Notes
Same registry as progression so dialogue/quests/puzzles check "can the player do X" regardless of source.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an item granting `verb.anchor-climb`, when equipped, then `hasCapability("verb.anchor-climb")` is true; when unequipped, it is false.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player already has a capability from progression and equips an item granting the same one, when the item is unequipped, then the capability remains (source-counted).
- AC-3 [integration] Given an equipped lantern, when the light field is sampled at the player position, then light level increases by the item's `lightRadius` contribution.
- AC-4 [integration] Given soft boots equipped, when the player walks on stone, then emitted footstep noise is reduced by the item's `noiseModifier`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an item granting an unknown capability at runtime (content bypass), when equipped, then equip succeeds, the grant is skipped and an error event is logged.

items.title: Build inventory screen with category tabs, inspect and actions
items.description:
## Why
The m1 loop includes loot; players need to see, inspect and use what they found with minimal friction.
## What
As a player, I want an inventory screen organized by category where I can inspect, equip, use, drop and assign items to quick slots so that managing gear takes seconds.

Tabs: All, Weapons & Armor, Tools, Consumables, Books, Keys, Quest & Artifacts. Item card shows icon, name, flavour description (room for QfG-style humour), granted verbs listed as verbs (not numbers first), stolen marker, value. Keyboard+mouse, gamepad navigation; respects text-size setting. Quick-slot HUD strip on the game screen.
## Scope
- In: Inventory screen, item inspect panel, context actions, quick-slot assignment, quick-slot HUD, placeholder icons by category
- Out: Paper-doll equipment view (e17-equipment-ui)
- Out: Final icon art (asset prompt beads)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: item category placeholder icons, stolen marker icon, gold icon, quick-slot frame, inventory panel frame. Final icons via asset group.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an inventory with items in 4 categories, when the Books tab is selected, then only book items are listed, sorted by acquisition time descending.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a stolen item, when its card is displayed, then the stolen marker is visible and the tooltip names the owner if known.
- AC-3 [integration] Given gamepad input only, when navigating the grid and pressing confirm on a consumable, then a context menu with Use/Assign/Drop opens and each action works.
- AC-4 [unit] Given text size set to 150%, when the inventory renders, then item names wrap without overlapping and no text is clipped (DOM overflow check).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the player opens inventory, assigns a potion to quick slot 2 and closes inventory, then pressing the quick-slot-2 action consumes the potion.
- AC-6 [unit] Given an empty inventory, when opened, then an empty-state message is shown instead of an empty grid.

items.title: Add equipment paper-doll view with verb and stealth comparison
items.description:
## Why
Equipment choices should be legible as trade-offs in verbs, noise and light, not just damage numbers.
## What
As a player, I want to see what I'm wearing and how swapping gear changes my noise, light and available verbs so that I can dress for the job (stealthy thief vs. armored knight).

Paper-doll with slot silhouettes, compare panel showing deltas for noise, weight class, light, granted/lost verbs, and key combat values. Non-proficiency penalties shown clearly.
## Scope
- In: Equipment view, compare panel, slot filters, gamepad support
- Out: 3D character preview rendering (optional, render group later)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: slot silhouette icons (head, body, hands, feet, main, off, trinket, ammo, tool), comparison up/down indicators.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given heavy armor equipped and soft leather hovered, when comparing, then the panel shows noise decrease and weight class change using derived EquipmentState values.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an item that grants a verb, when hovered, then the compare panel lists the verb under "Gains"; unequipping an item lists its verbs under "Loses".
- AC-3 [integration] Given a sorcerer hovering plate armor, when compared, then the non-proficiency penalty is shown with a warning style.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an empty slot, when rendered, then its silhouette placeholder is displayed and is focusable for gamepad navigation.

items.title: Add debug console commands to give, remove and inspect items
items.description:
## Why
Fast content iteration and bug reproduction require spawning items without playing to them.
## What
Debug console commands: `item.give <id> [count] [--stolen owner]`, `item.remove`, `item.list [category]`, `equip <id>`, `gold <n>`, with id auto-complete from the item catalogue.
## Scope
- In: Commands, autocomplete, error messages
- Out: Loot/quest commands (their own epics)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the console, when `item.give healing-draught 3` runs, then the inventory gains 3 and the console prints the new count.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an unknown item id, when `item.give` runs, then the console prints the 3 closest ids by edit distance and changes nothing.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `item.give silver-ring 1 --stolen mayor`, when executed, then the added instance has stolen=true and ownerId=mayor.

items.title: Implement loot table schema and deterministic seeded roller
items.description:
## Why
Loot is data (contract §1) and must be deterministic for replay tests; tables let designers favour handcrafted guarantees over random stat-sticks.
## What
As a designer, I want to author loot tables with guaranteed and weighted entries so that containers and creatures yield intentional discoveries.

Schema: `id`, `guaranteed: [{item, count}]`, `rolls: {min,max}`, `entries: [{item | table, weight, count:{min,max}, conditions?}]`, `noDuplicates`. Roller takes the seeded RNG stream + context (player class, world facts) and returns item stacks. Nested tables supported with depth limit 4. Unique items can only drop if not already in world state as obtained.
## Scope
- In: Schema + zod types, roller, uniqueness check against world state, conditional entries using simple predicates (class, fact) until the DSL lands
- Out: Containers (e18-containers)
- Out: Creature drops (e18-creature-drops)
- Out: Validator (e18-loot-validator)
## Notes
Conditions migrate to the shared DSL (e22-condition-effect-dsl) when available; keep the predicate interface identical.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a table with 2 guaranteed items and 0 rolls, when rolled with any seed, then exactly those 2 items are returned.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same table, seed and context, when rolled 10,000 times in two runs, then both result sequences are identical.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a weighted table (weights 3:1) rolled 40,000 times with seeded RNG, then observed ratios are within ±2% of 75%/25%.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a unique item already marked obtained in world state, when a table containing it is rolled, then the entry is skipped and its weight redistributed.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an entry conditioned on class `thief`, when rolled for a knight, then that entry never appears.
- AC-6 [unit] Given nested tables exceeding depth 4 at runtime, when rolled, then rolling stops at depth 4 and an error event is emitted (no infinite loop).

items.title: Validate loot tables: references, uniques, cycles, weights
items.description:
## Why
Broken loot data silently produces empty chests or duplicate artifacts; CI must catch it.
## What
Content validator run in CI over all loot tables and placements: all item/table references exist, weights > 0, count ranges valid, no cycles in nested tables, each unique item appears in at most one guaranteed placement across the world, every table is referenced by something (warning).
## Scope
- In: Validator module + CLI entry + CI hook via content pipeline
- Out: Balance analysis (e18-treasure-audit-tool)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a table referencing a missing item id, when validated, then validation fails naming the table, entry index and missing id.
- AC-2 [unit] Given tables A→B→A, when validated, then validation fails reporting the cycle path "A > B > A".
- AC-3 [unit] Given a unique artifact guaranteed in two placements, when validated, then validation fails listing both placements.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unreferenced table, when validated, then a warning (not an error) is reported.
- AC-5 [content] Given the repository's loot content, when CI runs the validator, then it exits 0.

items.title: Add lootable containers that persist their contents
items.description:
## Why
The m1 loop requires loot; the constitution says bookshelves, chests and wells should contain things, and looted state must persist.
## What
As a player, I want to open chests, barrels, bookshelves and corpses and take what's inside so that exploring pays off.

Container component: `contents` either fixed list or `lootTable` rolled once on first open (seed derived from container id + world seed so it is stable across reloads). Take one / take all, put items back. Hooks: `lockId` (e03), `trapId` (mw-e10), `ownerId` (e18-ownership-stolen). Contents persisted via world-state store after first open.
## Scope
- In: Container component, open/take/put, roll-once semantics, persistence, lock hook, empty-state
- Out: Container UI (e18-container-ui)
- Out: Trap mechanics (mw-e10)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an unopened container with a loot table, when opened twice across a save/reload, then the contents are identical both times (rolled once).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a container, when the player takes all, then contents move to inventory, container becomes empty and `container.looted` fact is set.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a locked container without a key, when opened, then it refuses with reason `locked` and does not roll its table.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player puts an item into a container, when saved and reloaded, then the item is still inside.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox testbed chest, when the player loots it, saves, reloads and opens it again, then it is empty.

items.title: Build container window and loot pickup notifications
items.description:
## Why
Discoveries need a moment of presentation; looting should be one or two inputs.
## What
As a player, I want a compact container window with Take / Take All and a short pickup toast so that looting is fast and discoveries feel noticed.

Container window lists contents with icons; Take All bound to a single key/button. Pickup toasts stack in a corner (max 4, merged by def). Unique artifacts get a distinct "discovery" toast with the item's flavour line.
## Scope
- In: Container window, take/take-all, pickup toasts, artifact discovery toast, gamepad support
- Out: Item inspection details (e17-inventory-ui)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: container window frame, pickup toast frame, artifact discovery banner.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an open container with 3 items, when Take All is pressed, then all 3 are in inventory and the window closes within the same frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given 6 items picked up within 1 second, when toasts display, then at most 4 toasts are visible and duplicates by def are merged with a count.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a unique artifact picked up, when displayed, then the discovery toast shows its flavour line and remains for ≥ 4 s.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an empty container, when opened, then the window shows "Empty" and Take All is disabled.

items.title: Support designer-placed and hidden treasure with discovery rules
items.description:
## Why
The world rewards curiosity: wells hide tunnels, loose bricks hide stashes. Handcrafted placement beats random drops.
## What
As a designer, I want to place specific items in the level and optionally hide them behind discovery conditions so that curious players find hand-authored rewards.

Placement data: `{id, itemOrTable, transform, hidden?: {revealWhen: property-based conditions}}`. Reveal conditions are systemic: light level above threshold (e03-light-field), capability present (e.g. `sense.detect-magic`), object moved/broken (e03 events). Looted placements persist.
## Scope
- In: Placement schema, reveal condition evaluation, persistence, greybox examples: stash under a movable crate, item only visible in light
- Out: Hidden passages / secret doors (mw-e03 / mw-e15)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a hidden placement with `revealWhen: lightLevel >= 0.6`, when light at its position rises to 0.7, then it becomes interactable and a `treasure.revealed` event fires once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a placement hidden under a movable object, when the object is moved off its footprint, then the placement is revealed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a looted placement, when the level reloads, then the placement does not respawn.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a reveal condition referencing an unknown capability, when content is validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Track item ownership and flag stolen items on witnessed theft
items.description:
## Why
Stealing must be a real systemic act with consequences (thief fantasy, Elder Scrolls living world) and feed shops, disposition and AI.
## What
As a thief, I want taking things that belong to others to be tracked and only punished when someone notices so that careful theft pays off and sloppy theft creates stories.

Ownership on containers, placements and world items (`ownerId` NPC or faction). Taking an owned item marks the instance `stolen` with owner. At the moment of taking, witnesses are evaluated via e11 perception/e09 visibility: witnessed theft emits `crime.theft` (value, owner, witnesses) consumed by e11-alert-states and disposition; unwitnessed theft emits nothing but the item remains flagged. Owner discovers missing high-value items later (optional fact `owner.noticedMissing`).
## Scope
- In: Ownership data, stolen flag assignment, witness check, crime event, returning stolen items clears the flag
- Out: Guard responses/bounty (mw-e11)
- Out: Fence pricing (e20-fences-stolen-goods)
- Out: Pickpocket minigame (mw-e10)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an owned item in a container and no witness able to see the player, when taken, then the instance is stolen with the ownerId and no `crime.theft` event is emitted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an NPC with the player in sight cone and visibility ≥ its threshold, when an owned item is taken, then `crime.theft` is emitted listing that NPC as witness.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stolen item given back to its owner (via dialogue effect or putting it back in the owner's container), when returned, then the stolen flag clears.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unowned item, when taken in full view, then no stolen flag or crime event occurs.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox guard watching a chest, when the player takes an item, then the guard enters at least the Suspicious alert state.

items.title: Drop what creatures actually carry, plus data-driven extras
items.description:
## Why
Creatures are not target dummies or loot piñatas; what they carry should be visible and plausible (the goblin with the lantern drops the lantern).
## What
As a player, I want defeated or robbed creatures to hold the gear I saw them using so that loot feels grounded.

Creature schema extension: `carried` inventory (equipped items shown on the creature) + optional `dropTable` for pouch contents. On death the corpse becomes a container; on pickpocket (mw-e10) the carried inventory is the source. Wolves drop nothing but pelts-as-quest-materials only if data says so.
## Scope
- In: Carried inventory on creatures, corpse-as-container, owned-by-creature flags (robbing a living goblin is theft)
- Out: Pickpocket mechanics (mw-e10)
- Out: Harvesting/crafting (not planned for MVP)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with carried [rusty-sword, lantern], when killed, then its corpse container holds exactly those plus the rolled drop table results.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature with no carried items and no drop table, when killed, then no corpse container is created (no empty loot prompt).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a living intelligent creature, when an item is taken from it, then the item is flagged stolen with the creature as owner.
- AC-4 [content] Given every creature data file, when validated, then all carried/dropTable references resolve.

items.title: Add unique artifacts with active verbs and lore
items.description:
## Why
Handcrafted discoveries with verbs are the reward that replaces stat-sticks; artifacts should make players say "wait, I can do that?"
## What
As a player, I want rare artifacts that do strange, useful things so that finding one changes how I play.

Artifact = item with `flags.unique` and either passive `grants` or an `activate` block (cooldown/charges, effects via the shared effect vocabulary and world properties). Examples for grey-box tests only: a compass that points to the nearest hidden placement, a bell that emits a loud noise event at a distance, a cold stone that gives `frozen` to touched water. Uniqueness enforced world-wide.
## Scope
- In: Activate verb, charges/cooldown, uniqueness guarantee, lore text field, 3 grey-box test artifacts
- Out: The MVP artifact roster (world-content group)
## Notes
Artifacts must express effects via properties (e03) — never artifact-specific code paths.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an artifact with 3 charges and recharge-on-rest, when activated 4 times without rest, then the 4th activation fails with reason `no-charges`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a unique artifact already obtained, when any table or placement tries to grant another, then no second instance is created.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the bell test artifact activated, when resolved, then a noise event with the configured loudness is emitted at the target point and nearby guards react via e11.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the cold-stone test artifact touching a `wet`/water volume, when resolved, then the volume gains `frozen` via e03 propagation.
- AC-5 [content] Given all artifact data, when validated, then each has a non-empty lore text key and at least one grant or activate effect.

items.title: Write treasure design guide for handcrafted loot
items.description:
## Why
World-content authors need a shared rule set so loot stays meaningful across the town, wilderness and labyrinth.
## What
docs/design/treasure.md: treasure tiers (junk-with-jokes, useful consumables, tools, books, artifacts), placement density guidelines ("interesting-looking places usually contain something"), ratio of handcrafted vs table-rolled, gold budget per area (links to economy doc), ownership conventions, humour guidelines for flavour text.
## Scope
- In: Guide doc with examples and anti-patterns
- Out: Actual placements (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the guide, when reviewed, then it defines each treasure tier with one example and an anti-pattern.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the guide, when reviewed, then it states numeric density targets (e.g. discoveries per room/area) and the handcrafted:rolled ratio.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the guide, when reviewed, then it references the economy gold budget from e20-economy-design.

items.title: Build treasure audit and loot distribution report tool
items.description:
## Why
Designers need to see what a region yields before playtesting it, and to catch gold inflation or missing books.
## What
CLI `pnpm content:loot-report [region]`: enumerates placements, containers and creature drops; simulates each table N times (seeded) and outputs expected gold, item counts by category, unique artifact locations, and per-class availability of progression items (books, tools, schematics). Debug console command `loot.roll <table> [n]`.
## Scope
- In: CLI report (markdown + JSON), console command
- Out: Economy balance CI gate (e20-economy-balance-tool)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture region with 2 containers and known tables, when the report runs with seed 1 and N=1000, then expected gold equals the analytic expectation within ±1%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a region where a class-gated progression item has no source, when the report runs, then it lists that item under "Unobtainable".
- AC-3 [unit] Given `loot.roll unknown-table`, when executed in the console, then it reports an error and suggests close matches.

items.title: Spike: capability-unlock progression model, stats and respec policy
items.description:
## Why
The anti-grind rule demands progression that unlocks verbs, not numbers. We must decide the model before class, loot and shop data are authored against it.
## What
Time-box: 1.5 days. Questions: (1) Is there XP/levels at all, or do unlocks come only from in-world sources (books, trainers, schematics, tools, deeds)? (2) Which minimal supporting stats exist (health, stamina, focus/mana) and how do they grow (found items, shrines, deeds)? (3) How does each class earn verbs: sorcerer books, knight trainer techniques, archer arrows + trick-shot techniques, thief tools + tricks? (4) Can classes cross-learn (a knight reading a simple spellbook)? (5) Respec policy: none (additive capabilities), loadout swapping, or paid retraining?
## Scope
- In: ADR with recommendation, per-class unlock channel table, stat list with ranges, respec decision, anti-grind validation rules for content
- Out: Implementation (e19-capability-registry onward)
## Notes
Leaning: no XP; unlocks are in-world acquisitions; supporting stats grow via rare found items/deeds; capabilities are additive so respec is limited to loadout choices (e.g. prepared spell slots) — revisit if playtests disagree.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the spike, when complete, then docs/adr/ contains an Accepted progression ADR answering all five questions.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it contains a table listing each class's unlock channels with at least 3 example verb chains per class following the Firebolt → Flame Jet → Fire Wall pattern.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it lists the supporting stats (≤ 5) with numeric start values and caps.
- AC-4 [manual] Given the ADR, when read, then it defines content validation rules that reject pure numeric-upgrade unlocks unless flagged `supporting`.

items.title: Create capability registry with source-tracked grants
items.description:
## Why
Dialogue, quests, puzzles, interaction prompts and equipment all ask "can the player do X?"; one registry avoids class checks scattered through code.
## What
Capability definitions as data (`id` like `verb.climb.ledge`, `spell.ember`, `arrow.rope`, `tool.lockpick`, `sense.detect-magic`; `nameKey`, `descKey`, `icon`, `class` affinity, `supporting` flag). Runtime registry per actor: `grant(capId, source)`, `revoke(capId, source)`, `has(capId)`, `sources(capId)`, reference-counted by source (`class`, `learned`, `equipment:<id>`, `temporary:<effectId>`). Emits `capability.gained` / `capability.lost` only on 0↔1 transitions.
## Scope
- In: Capability schema + validator, registry runtime, events, query API
- Out: Unlock rules and prerequisites (e19-progression-core)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a capability granted by two sources, when one source revokes it, then `has` is still true and no `capability.lost` event is emitted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a capability with zero sources, when granted, then exactly one `capability.gained` event is emitted.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a grant of an undefined capability id, when called, then it throws in dev/test builds and is a logged no-op in production builds.
- AC-4 [content] Given the capability data files, when validated, then ids are unique and match the pattern `^(verb|spell|arrow|tool|trick|technique|sense)\.[a-z0-9.-]+$`.

items.title: Implement capability-unlock progression with prerequisite chains
items.description:
## Why
Progression should unlock new verbs (constitution §3). This is the rule engine every class channel plugs into.
## What
As a player, I want each thing I learn to give me a new way to act, building on what I already know, so that my character grows in possibilities rather than numbers.

Unlock definitions: `{capability, prerequisites: [capIds], requirements: conditions, source channel}`. `learn(capId, channel)` checks prerequisites and requirements and grants with source `learned`. Supports verb chains (Firebolt → Flame Jet → Fire Wall) and upgrades that *replace or extend* a verb (Telekinesis → throw creatures). Learned set persists via save.
## Scope
- In: Unlock definitions schema, learn API, prerequisite resolution, "why can't I learn this" explanations, save section
- Out: Class-specific channels (e19-*-channel items)
- Out: UI (e19-capabilities-screen)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `spell.flame-jet` requiring `spell.ember`, when a player without Ember tries to learn Flame Jet, then learning fails with reason `missing-prerequisite: spell.ember`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given all prerequisites met, when learned, then the capability is granted with source `learned` and `progression.learned` is emitted with the channel.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a capability already learned, when learned again, then the call is a no-op returning `already-known` (no duplicate events).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unlock that `replaces` a previous capability, when learned, then the old capability's `learned` source is revoked and the new one granted atomically.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a learned set, when saved and loaded, then the registry state is identical.
- AC-6 [content] Given all unlock definitions, when validated, then there are no prerequisite cycles and no unlock is a pure numeric upgrade unless flagged `supporting`.

items.title: Define the four classes as data: kit, capabilities, proficiencies
items.description:
## Why
Classes change possibilities; defining them as data keeps class checks out of code and makes dialogue/quest gating uniform.
## What
Class schema + four class files (knight, archer, sorcerer, thief): `startingCapabilities`, `startingKit` (items, gold), `proficiencies` (weight classes, weapon tags), `supportingStats` start values, `dialogueTag` (for [Thief]-style options), `unlockChannels` (which progression channels apply), `iconId`, `portraitId`. Grey-box starting kits only; final kits tuned later.
## Scope
- In: Class schema, 4 class data files with placeholder kits, validator
- Out: Selection UI (e19-class-selection)
- Out: Final starting kits (tuned during m2/m3)

**Integration note:** Archer class data should grant `sense.tracking` (used by the Sleepers' Path in E25 to reveal sleepwalker trails in daylight); if not granted, the path falls back to night-only visibility.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 4 class files, when validated, then each has ≥ 2 starting capabilities, a starting kit whose items all resolve, and a unique dialogueTag.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a class whose startingCapabilities include an id not in the registry, when validated, then validation fails naming the class and id.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a class file with no unlock channel, when validated, then validation fails (every class must be able to progress).

items.title: Add class selection at new game that applies kit and capabilities
items.description:
## Why
Choosing a class is the game's core promise; the choice must be clear and apply fully at start.
## What
As a player, I want to choose Knight, Archer, Sorcerer or Thief at the start and see what each can do so that I pick the fantasy I want.

New-game flow: class cards with short pitch, 3 signature verbs listed, starting kit preview. Confirm applies class: grants starting capabilities (source `class`), adds kit to inventory, equips kit, sets stats. Class stored in save and exposed to conditions (`player.class`).
## Scope
- In: Selection screen (grey-box styling), apply-class sim function, save field, keyboard/gamepad navigation
- Out: Character customization/appearance (not MVP)
- Out: Final class card art (asset group)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: 4 class card illustrations/portraits, 4 class emblem icons.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the thief class applied to a fresh player, when complete, then the registry, inventory and equipment exactly match the thief data file.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the selection screen, when the player tries to confirm without a class highlighted, then confirm is disabled.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a new game, when the player selects Sorcerer and enters the greybox testbed, then the HUD shows the sorcerer starting kit and `player.class` is `sorcerer`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given apply-class is called on a player who already has a class, when executed, then it throws `class-already-set` (no stacking of classes).

items.title: Implement minimal supporting stats and rare stat growth sources
items.description:
## Why
Stats can exist but must support rather than define progression (constitution §3); keep them few and legible.
## What
As a player, I want a small set of stats (e.g. health, stamina, focus) that grow from rare discoveries so that finding a heart-container-like relic feels special without turning into grind.

Stats per ADR (≤ 5), with base from class, modifiers from equipment and temporary effects, and permanent increments from data-defined sources (relic items, shrines, deeds). Hard caps. No per-kill XP.
## Scope
- In: Stat model with base/modifier/permanent layers, caps, sources, events, save section
- Out: Combat consumption of stamina/poise (mw-e04)
- Out: Mana/focus spending (mw-e06)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given base health 100 and a relic granting +10 permanent max health, when consumed, then max health is 110 and current health increases by 10.
- AC-2 [unit] Given max health at its cap, when another permanent increment is applied, then it is clamped and the source is not consumed (returns `at-cap`).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an equipment modifier of -10 stamina, when unequipped, then stamina max returns to its prior value.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature is killed, when resolved, then no stat changes occur (no per-kill XP).

items.title: Wire spellbook learning into progression prerequisites
items.description:
## Why
Magic is learned primarily from books (constitution §4). Book learning must respect progression prerequisites and class rules defined in the ADR.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want reading a spellbook to teach me its spell when I understand the prerequisites so that books become exciting and school knowledge matters.

Adapter from e07-spellbook-learning to `progression.learn(spell, channel: book)`. Handles: missing prerequisite (book stays readable, shows what knowledge is missing), non-sorcerer readers per ADR cross-learning rule, damaged/untranslated books gated by conditions.
## Scope
- In: Adapter, failure explanations, cross-class rule enforcement
- Out: Book reading UI and spell data (mw-e07, mw-e08)
- Out: Bookshop inventories (e21-bookshop-system)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sorcerer reading a book for a spell whose prerequisites are met, when read, then the spell capability is granted with source `learned` and channel `book`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a knight reading a sorcerer-only spellbook, when read, then no capability is granted and the result explains per ADR (e.g. "The runes swim before your eyes.").
- AC-3 [unit] Given a book whose spell is already known, when read, then no duplicate grant occurs and the book is flagged `read`.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the greybox testbed, when a sorcerer picks up and reads a test spellbook, then the new spell appears in the capabilities list and can be cast.

items.title: Let trainers teach knight techniques through dialogue services
items.description:
## Why
Knights master techniques; learning them from a character (for gold, a deed, or a duel) is more memorable than a skill point.
## What
As a knight, I want to learn new techniques from trainers who demand payment, proof or a test so that each new move has a story.

Trainer = NPC with `teaches: [{capability, price?, requires: conditions, test?: questId}]`. Dialogue effect `learnCapability` (via e22 DSL) and a service listing in the trainer's dialogue. Supports technique chains (shield bash → shield charge → shield vault) and non-gold prices (a favour quest).
## Scope
- In: Trainer data schema, dialogue effect binding, gold deduction via shop transactions, test-quest gating
- Out: Technique mechanics (mw-e04)
- Out: Specific trainer NPCs (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a trainer teaching `technique.shield-charge` for 50 gold and a knight with 60 gold and the prerequisite, when learned, then gold is 10 and the capability is granted with channel `trainer`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given insufficient gold, when the learn effect runs, then it fails atomically (no gold removed, no capability).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a technique gated by a test quest not yet resolved, when offered in dialogue, then the option is shown as locked with its requirement text.
- AC-4 [content] Given all trainer data, when validated, then every taught capability exists and every test quest id resolves.

items.title: Unlock archer trick arrows via schematics and trick-shot techniques
items.description:
## Why
Archers control space through specialized arrows and trick shots; new arrow types are new verbs.
## What
As an archer, I want to find fletching schematics and learn trick shots so that my quiver gains new ways to solve problems (rope arrows, water arrows, noise arrows).

Fletching schematic item → `learn(arrow.<type>, channel: schematic)`; once known, arrows of that type can be assembled at rest points from simple materials (count-limited, no crafting tree). Trick-shot techniques (e.g. ricochet, pinning) learned from deeds or trainers via the shared channels.
## Scope
- In: Schematic item handling, simple arrow assembly (materials → arrows), trick-shot unlock via deed/trainer
- Out: Arrow physics and effects (mw-e05)
- Out: General crafting system (not MVP)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an archer reading a rope-arrow schematic, when read, then `arrow.rope` is learned with channel `schematic` and the schematic is consumed.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `arrow.rope` known and 2 rope + 2 shafts, when assembling at a rest point, then 2 rope arrows are added and materials removed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `arrow.rope` not known, when assembling, then the recipe is unavailable even with materials.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a non-archer reading a schematic, when read, then behaviour follows the ADR cross-learning rule and is covered by a test.

items.title: Grant thief verbs from tools and tricks learned from contacts
items.description:
## Why
Thief growth is about tools and tricks (lockpicks, grapples, smoke, disguises); owning a tool is owning a verb.
## What
As a thief, I want new tools and tricks to open new routes so that my arsenal grows in options, not numbers.

Tools are items with `grants` (via e17-equipment-verbs on the toolBelt, or passive when carried per ADR). Tricks (e.g. `trick.feign-death`, `trick.shadow-step`) are learned from notes/contacts via the shared learn API with channel `trick`. Tool degradation per ADR (e.g. lockpicks can break — failure creates stories).
## Scope
- In: Tool-carried capability grants, trick learning channel, optional breakage rule hook
- Out: Tool mechanics (mw-e10)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given lockpicks on the tool belt, when checked, then `tool.lockpick` is granted; removing the lockpicks revokes it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a trick note read by a thief, when read, then the trick is learned with channel `trick`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a breakable tool with 1 durability, when a breaking event occurs, then the tool is removed and its capability revoked with a `tool.broke` event.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two lockpick stacks, when one breaks, then the capability remains while any stack remains.

items.title: Unlock capabilities from notable deeds via data-driven rules
items.description:
## Why
Some verbs are best earned by doing something memorable (befriending the minotaur, surviving a fall into the mine), rewarding curiosity instead of repetition.
## What
As a player, I want remarkable actions to teach me something so that the world itself trains me.

Deed rules: `{when: event/fact conditions, grants: capability, once: true, message}` evaluated on world-state changes. Explicitly not repetition counters (anti-grind): validator rejects deed rules whose condition is a count > 3 of the same event unless flagged.
## Scope
- In: Deed rule schema, evaluator on world-state/event bus, validator anti-grind rule, notification event
- Out: Specific deeds (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a deed rule on fact `minotaur.befriended`, when the fact becomes true, then the capability is learned with channel `deed` exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the fact toggles false then true again, when evaluated, then the deed does not grant twice.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a deed rule requiring 20 kills of the same creature type without `allowRepetition`, when validated, then validation fails citing the anti-grind rule.

items.title: Build capabilities screen and "new verb learned" feedback
items.description:
## Why
Players must notice and remember new verbs, otherwise capability progression is invisible.
## What
As a player, I want a screen listing what I can do, grouped by source, with hints about what I might learn next, and a clear moment when I learn something new so that I try my new verbs.

Screen: capabilities grouped (Class, Learned, From Gear, Temporary), each with icon, description and input hint. "Rumoured" section shows known-but-unlearned capabilities from rumors/books glimpsed. Learn moment: banner with verb name, one-line usage hint, and input glyph; optional short practice prompt.
## Scope
- In: Capabilities screen, learn banner, input glyph binding, rumoured hints
- Out: Spellbook-specific UI (mw-e07)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: capability/verb icons per class (placeholder shapes first), learn banner frame, input glyph set (KB/M + gamepad).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given capabilities from class, learning and an equipped lantern, when the screen opens, then each appears under the correct group with its icon.
- AC-2 [integration] Given `capability.gained` from a learn action, when fired, then the learn banner appears within 1 frame and shows the currently bound input glyph for that verb.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player remaps the verb's input, when the screen reopens, then the new glyph is shown.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a temporary capability expires while the screen is open, when it expires, then it is removed from the list without closing the screen.

items.title: Implement respec/loadout policy decided in the progression ADR
items.description:
## Why
Experimentation is a pillar; if any capability choices are exclusive, players need a fair way to change them.
## What
As a player, I want to adjust my loadout of prepared capabilities (per ADR) so that I can experiment without restarting.

Implements whatever the ADR chose: expected default is loadout slots (e.g. prepared spells / equipped techniques) swappable at rest points, with no destructive respec because learned capabilities are additive.
## Scope
- In: Loadout slots per ADR, swap rules, rest-point integration, save section
- Out: Anything the ADR rejects
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a loadout of N slots full, when a new capability is slotted at a rest point, then the displaced one returns to the known pool (never lost).
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player is not at a rest point, when a swap is requested, then it fails with reason `not-at-rest` if the ADR requires rest.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a slotted capability later revoked (e.g. source item lost), when revoked, then its slot empties and an event is emitted.

items.title: Write economy design: gold income, meaningful sinks, price bands
items.description:
## Why
Gold must have meaningful uses; without a budget the MVP will either drown the player in gold or starve the bookshop.
## What
docs/design/economy.md: gold income sources (loot, quests, selling, theft), meaningful sinks (spellbooks, trainer techniques, arrow materials, thief tools, services, bribes, donations/deeds), price bands per item tier, target gold curve across the MVP (e.g. can afford 1 of 3 premium books on first bookshop visit), merchant markup ranges, disposition and stolen-goods modifier ranges, haggle limits.
## Scope
- In: Doc with numeric targets consumed by e20-price-model and e20-economy-balance-tool
- Out: Merchant content (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the doc, when reviewed, then it lists every sink category with a price band in gold.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the doc, when reviewed, then it defines a target obtainable-gold : sink-cost ratio band for the MVP region (e.g. 0.6–0.8) used by the balance tool.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the doc, when reviewed, then it gives numeric ranges for disposition, specialty, stolen and haggle modifiers.

items.title: Define merchant schema with identity, specialty and stock rules
items.description:
## Why
Merchants need identities, inventories and specialties (QfG5 personality, Elder Scrolls living shops) authored as data.
## What
Zod schema `merchant`: `id`, `npcId` (dialogue speaker), `personalityTags` (e.g. greedy, gossipy, suspicious), `specialties` (item categories/tags bought at better rates), `buysCategories`, `stock: [{item | lootTable, count, restock?}]`, `goldReserve` + `goldRestock`, `markup`/`buyRate` bands, `isFence`, `hours?` (world time hook), `barkSet` id. Validator checks references and bands against economy doc.
## Scope
- In: Schema, validator, 2 grey-box fixture merchants (general goods, fence)
- Out: Bookshop specialisation (e21-bookshop-system extends this)
- Out: Briar Glen merchants (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 2 fixture merchants, when validated, then validation passes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a merchant with markup outside the economy doc band, when validated, then validation fails naming merchant and field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a merchant whose stock references a missing item or loot table, when validated, then validation fails with the reference.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a merchant with `isFence: false` and `buysStolen: true`, when validated, then validation fails (only fences buy stolen goods).

items.title: Implement pure price model with disposition and stolen modifiers
items.description:
## Why
Prices must respond to relationships and context, be deterministic, and be 100% tested (contract §3: economy at 100%).
## What
Pure function `price({item, instance, merchant, direction: buy|sell, disposition, haggleModifier, worldFacts})` → integer gold with a breakdown of applied modifiers. Modifiers: base value, merchant markup/buyRate, specialty bonus, disposition band multiplier, stolen (fence discount; non-fence refuses), quest items unsellable, floor of 1 gold, sell price never exceeds buy price for the same merchant.
## Scope
- In: Price function, breakdown for UI, exhaustive tests incl. property tests
- Out: Transactions (e20-shop-system)
- Out: Haggle flow (e20-haggling)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an item of value 100, merchant markup 1.2 and neutral disposition, when pricing a buy, then the price is 120 and the breakdown lists base and markup.
- AC-2 [unit] Given friendly vs cold disposition bands, when pricing the same buy, then the friendly price is lower by the economy doc multipliers.
- AC-3 [unit] Given any item/merchant/disposition combination (property test, 10,000 cases), when pricing, then sell price ≤ buy price and price ≥ 1.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a stolen item and a non-fence merchant, when pricing a sell, then the result is `refused: stolen`.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a quest item, when pricing a sell, then the result is `refused: quest-item`.

items.title: Implement merchant buy/sell transactions with persistent stock
items.description:
## Why
Gold needs meaningful uses and merchants need living inventories; transactions must never duplicate or lose items or gold.
## What
As a player, I want to buy and sell with merchants whose stock and gold are finite and remembered so that shops feel like real places.

Atomic transactions: buy (player gold ≥ price, stock > 0) and sell (merchant gold ≥ price, merchant buys category, not refused). Buyback: last 10 sold items repurchasable at the sell price until restock. Stock, gold and buyback stored in world-state store. Emits `shop.bought`/`shop.sold` events for quests/telemetry.
## Scope
- In: Transaction engine, merchant runtime state, buyback, persistence, events
- Out: Restocking (e20-restock-rotation)
- Out: UI (e20-shop-ui)
- Out: Haggling (e20-haggling)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given player gold 100 and an item priced 80 with stock 1, when bought, then player gold is 20, the item is in inventory, merchant gold +80 and stock 0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given stock 0, when a buy is attempted, then it fails with `out-of-stock` and no state changes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given merchant gold 30 and a sell priced 50, when sold, then it fails with `merchant-cannot-afford` (or offers 30 if the economy doc enables partial) and state is unchanged on failure.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an item just sold, when bought back before restock, then the price equals the sell price.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 1,000 random buy/sell sequences (seeded), when executed, then total gold across player+merchant and total item count are conserved.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a transaction, when saved and reloaded, then merchant stock, gold and buyback are unchanged.

items.title: Restock merchant inventories on world-time ticks deterministically
items.description:
## Why
Living shops change over time; rotating stock gives reasons to return (and underpins bookshop rotation in E21).
## What
As a player, I want merchants to restock and occasionally carry new things so that revisiting shops is worthwhile.

On world day tick: restock entries flagged `restock` up to their counts, roll `rotating` loot-table entries with seed (merchantId, day), refill gold toward reserve, clear buyback. Unique items never restock. Condition-gated stock (e.g. after a quest outcome) appears when conditions become true.
## Scope
- In: Restock scheduler, rotation rolling, conditional stock, gold refill
- Out: Bookshop regional/rare/secret rules (e21-bookshop-system)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a restock entry of count 3 with stock 0, when a day tick passes, then stock is 3.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same merchant and day, when rotation rolls twice (e.g. across reload), then the rotating stock is identical.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sold-out unique item, when any number of day ticks pass, then it never reappears.
- AC-4 [unit] Given stock gated on fact `bridge.repaired`, when the fact becomes true, then the entry appears on the next tick.

items.title: Support fences and merchant reactions to stolen goods
items.description:
## Why
Stolen goods need an outlet and consequences; offering a merchant their own stolen silver should be memorable (and funny).
## What
As a thief, I want to sell stolen goods to a fence at a discount, and face consequences if I try to sell them to their owner so that theft is a complete loop.

Fences buy stolen items at the economy-doc discount. Non-fences refuse stolen items; if the merchant (or their faction) is the owner, emit `crime.theft.recognized` → disposition drop and optional guard alert. Fences can "launder" at a fee (clear stolen flag) if the design doc enables it.
## Scope
- In: Fence rules, owner recognition, disposition/crime events, optional laundering
- Out: Guard arrest/bounty behaviour (mw-e11)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a stolen item worth 100 and a fence with discount 0.4, when sold, then the player receives the price model result for a fence (breakdown includes stolen discount).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a merchant who owns a stolen item the player tries to sell, when attempted, then the sale is refused, disposition drops by the configured amount and `crime.theft.recognized` is emitted.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stolen item owned by someone else, when offered to a non-fence, then the sale is refused with no crime event.
- AC-4 [unit] Given laundering enabled, when paid, then the stolen flag clears and gold is deducted atomically.

items.title: Allow stealing shop stock with witness-based consequences
items.description:
## Why
Shops are prime thief targets; lifting an item from a counter while the merchant is distracted is a classic thief moment.
## What
As a thief, I want to steal displayed wares or from the merchant's stock when unobserved so that distractions and timing pay off.

Shop display items are world items owned by the merchant; taking them uses e18 ownership + witness checks. Witnessed shoplifting: merchant disposition drop, prices up, possible ban (`merchant.banned` fact) and guard alert. Stolen shop stock decrements merchant stock.
## Scope
- In: Display items bound to merchant stock, consequences ladder (warning → price hike → ban), ban lifting via fine/quest effect
- Out: Pickpocketing the merchant (mw-e10)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an unwitnessed theft of a displayed item, when taken, then merchant stock decrements and the instance is stolen with owner = merchant.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a first witnessed theft, when detected, then the consequence ladder moves to "warning" and disposition drops per data.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a banned merchant, when the player opens the shop, then trade is refused with a ban dialogue line until a `fine.paid` effect lifts the ban.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the greybox shop with a merchant facing away, when the thief takes a displayed item, then no crime event fires; facing toward, then one fires.

items.title: Add haggling with class options and disposition risk
items.description:
## Why
QfG-style merchant banter and DOS2 persuasion make trading a social encounter rather than a spreadsheet.
## What
As a player, I want to haggle a price using my class's strengths (knight's reputation, thief's bluff, sorcerer's impressive trick, archer's trade in pelts) so that talking well saves gold.

Haggle is a short dialogue sub-flow: choose an approach, deterministic check (disposition + class/capability modifiers + merchant personality), success grants a haggle modifier (bounded by the economy doc), failure worsens price or disposition; limited to 2 attempts per item per day.
## Scope
- In: Haggle flow via dialogue runtime, deterministic check formula, attempt limits, personality modifiers
- Out: General persuasion checks (e22-persuasion-checks is reused)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a greedy merchant and a thief bluff approach with modifiers summing above threshold, when haggling, then the price improves by the data-defined amount and never beyond the doc cap.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a failed haggle, when resolved, then disposition drops per personality data and the next haggle on that item has a penalty.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 2 attempts already made on an item today, when a third is requested, then the option is unavailable with the merchant's refusal line.
- AC-4 [unit] Given identical state, when the same haggle is attempted twice from the same save, then the outcome is identical (no hidden randomness).

items.title: Add purchasable services as meaningful gold sinks
items.description:
## Why
Gold has meaningful uses beyond items: healing, lodging, translation of books, bribes and donations create choices and stories.
## What
As a player, I want to pay for services (heal, rest at the inn, translate an untranslated book, bribe a guard, donate to the shrine) so that gold opens doors, not just inventory slots.

Service schema: `{id, providerNpcId, price or priceFormula, conditions, effects}` reusing the effect DSL; invoked from dialogue. Bribes/donations can change disposition or facts.
## Scope
- In: Service schema + validator, purchase via dialogue effect, atomic gold deduction
- Out: Trainer techniques (e19-knight-trainer-channel uses this)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a translate-book service costing 40 and an untranslated book in inventory, when purchased, then 40 gold is removed and the book instance gains `translated`.
- AC-2 [unit] Given insufficient gold, when purchasing, then nothing changes and the dialogue receives `insufficient-gold`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a service whose conditions are unmet (e.g. no untranslated book), when listed, then it is hidden or shown locked per its `showWhenLocked` flag.
- AC-4 [content] Given service data, when validated, then every provider NPC and effect reference resolves.

items.title: Build shop UI with merchant identity, buy/sell and price breakdown
items.description:
## Why
Merchants must feel like characters, and players must understand why prices are what they are.
## What
As a player, I want a shop screen that shows the merchant's face and personality, clear buy/sell lists and why an item costs what it does so that trading is quick and characterful.

Layout: merchant portrait slot + greeting bark; tabs Buy / Sell / Buyback / Services; item rows with price, specialty badge, stolen marker (sell tab), comparison vs equipped; price tooltip shows modifier breakdown (disposition, specialty, haggle); Haggle button (when available); quantity selector for stacks; confirm for expensive (> 25% of gold) purchases.
## Scope
