- In: Shop screen, tabs, breakdown tooltip, quantity selector, confirmation, keyboard/gamepad, text-size support
- Out: Haggle flow UI (uses dialogue UI)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: shop panel frame, merchant portrait frame, specialty badge icon, gold icon, stolen marker icon, buyback icon.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a merchant with specialty "books", when the Sell tab lists a book, then a specialty badge shows and the tooltip lists the specialty modifier.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a purchase costing > 25% of player gold, when confirmed, then a confirmation dialog appears; cheaper purchases complete in one input.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a stolen item on the Sell tab at a non-fence, when displayed, then the row is disabled with the refusal reason.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox merchant, when the player buys an item and sells it back via Buyback, then gold and inventory match the pre-buy state.
- AC-5 [unit] Given text size 150%, when the shop renders, then price columns remain aligned and no row text is clipped.

items.title: Add data-driven merchant barks for shop events
items.description:
## Why
Merchants with personality (QfG5) react to what you do — browsing forever, haggling badly, offering them their own candlestick.
## What
Bark sets keyed by shop event (`greet`, `browseLong`, `buyExpensive`, `sellJunk`, `haggleWin`, `haggleFail`, `stolenRecognized`, `banned`, `farewell`) with condition filters and anti-repetition (no same line twice within 5 uses). Uses e22 bark system for display.
## Scope
- In: Bark set schema for shop events, selection logic, 1 grey-box bark set
- Out: Actual merchant writing (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bark set with 3 greet lines, when greet fires 3 times, then 3 distinct lines are chosen before any repeats.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a `browseLong` threshold of 60 s in the shop UI, when exceeded, then exactly one browseLong bark is emitted.
- AC-3 [content] Given a bark set missing the `greet` event, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Add economy balance report and CI gate
items.description:
## Why
Balance drifts as content grows; a CI gate keeps gold meaningful without playtesting every change.
## What
CLI `pnpm content:economy-report`: sums expected obtainable gold (loot report + quest rewards + sellable items at average buy rates) vs total cost of meaningful sinks (books, techniques, tools, services) for the MVP region; fails CI if the ratio leaves the band in docs/design/economy.md. Outputs markdown report artifact.
## Scope
- In: Report CLI, CI step, markdown output
- Out: Loot distribution details (e18-treasure-audit-tool, reused)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given fixture content with known totals, when the report runs, then the computed ratio matches the analytic value.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a ratio outside the configured band, when run in CI mode, then the process exits non-zero naming the direction (too rich/too poor).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a quest with a gold reward effect, when the report runs, then it is included in obtainable gold.

items.title: Create shared typed condition/effect DSL for dialogue, quests, shops
items.description:
## Why
Dialogue, quests, shops, loot and deeds all need "if X then do Y" without bespoke scripting; one validated DSL prevents five incompatible mini-languages and eval().
## What
JSON-serializable, zod-validated expression language in src/sim/logic. Conditions: `all/any/not`, `fact`, `factCmp`, `hasItem`, `hasCapability`, `playerClass`, `disposition`, `questState`, `objectiveState`, `gold`, `timeOfDay`. Effects: `setFact`, `giveItem`, `takeItem`, `gold`, `disposition`, `startQuest`, `completeObjective`, `resolveQuest`, `failQuest`, `learnCapability`, `emit` (sim event), `revealRumor`. Evaluator is pure over a context interface; effects apply as an atomic batch (all or nothing). Extensible registry so other epics add condition/effect kinds with their own validators.
## Scope
- In: Schema, evaluator, atomic effect applier, registry for extension, reference validation hooks, human-readable describe() for tooling/UI
- Out: Dialogue graph (e22-dialogue-runtime)
- Out: Quest graph (e23-quest-runtime)
## Notes
No string expressions, no eval. Describe() output powers "requires: …" hints for locked options.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `all[hasItem(key-a), not(fact(door.open))]` and a context with key-a and door closed, when evaluated, then result is true.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an effect batch [takeItem(x), giveItem(y)] where takeItem fails, when applied, then neither effect is applied and the failure reason is returned.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an unknown condition kind in data, when validated, then validation fails naming the kind and path.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a registered extension condition, when used in content, then it validates and evaluates like built-ins.
- AC-5 [unit] Given any condition, when describe() is called, then it returns a non-empty localized-key string (tested for every built-in kind).

items.title: Define dialogue authoring format and schema
items.description:
## Why
Designers and writers must author conversations as data quickly, with humour and branching, without touching code.
## What
Dialogue file format (JSON or YAML compiled to JSON, decided here): `id`, `speakers`, `entry` nodes (multiple, conditioned — e.g. first meeting vs return), node kinds `line` (speaker, textKey/text, next), `choice` (options with text, conditions, `showWhenLocked`, class tag, effects, next), `branch` (conditional routing), `check` (persuasion; e22-persuasion-checks), `effect`, `jump` (to other dialogue), `end`. Text inline for MVP with stable ids for future localization. Supports `once` options and `visitedCount` conditions.
## Scope
- In: Format + zod schema, YAML→JSON compile step if chosen, 2 fixture dialogues, format doc section
- Out: Runtime (e22-dialogue-runtime)
- Out: Validator graph checks (e22-dialogue-validator)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 2 fixture dialogues, when compiled and validated, then they pass.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a node with an unknown `kind`, when validated, then validation fails with file, node id and line.
- AC-3 [unit] Given duplicate node ids within one dialogue, when validated, then validation fails listing both.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a choice option lacking both `next` and an `end` flag, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Track NPC disposition with bands, event modifiers and factions
items.description:
## Why
How characters feel about the player should change prices, dialogue options and help offered — the core of a reactive world.
## What
As a player, I want NPCs to remember how I treated them so that kindness, theft and bravado have social consequences.

Per-NPC disposition -100..100 with bands (hostile < -50, cold, neutral, friendly, devoted > 75). Sources: dialogue effects, gifts, witnessed crimes, quest outcomes, class affinity baseline. Optional light faction propagation (fraction of delta to faction members). Stored in world-state store. Emits `disposition.bandChanged`.
## Scope
- In: Disposition store, band mapping, event-driven modifiers (crime.theft, quest outcomes), faction propagation, save
- Out: Creature-level befriending (mw-e14)
- Out: AI hostility decisions (mw-e11 consumes bands)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given disposition 45 (neutral) and a +10 effect, when applied, then disposition is 55, band becomes friendly and one `disposition.bandChanged` event fires.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a +200 effect, when applied, then disposition clamps at 100.
- AC-3 [unit] Given faction propagation 0.5 and a -20 delta to one member, when applied, then other faction members receive -10.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a `crime.theft` event naming a witness who is the owner, when processed, then the owner's disposition drops by the configured theft amount scaled by item value tier.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an NPC never met, when queried, then it returns the class-affinity baseline from data (default 0).

items.title: Implement dialogue graph runtime with conditions and effects
items.description:
## Why
Characters support conversations, choices and lightweight state tracking without bespoke code (E22 outcome).
## What
As a designer, I want authored dialogues to run deterministically with conditions, effects and memory so that NPCs react to what the player has done.

Runtime in src/sim/dialogue: `start(dialogueId, npcId)` picks the first entry whose conditions pass; steps through nodes; `getChoices()` returns available options (+ locked ones with describe() reasons when `showWhenLocked`); `choose(i)` applies effects atomically and advances; tracks visited nodes/options per NPC in world state (`once` options disappear); `end` or abort (combat interrupt) leaves consistent state. Emits `dialogue.started/nodeVisited/ended` events for quests.
## Scope
- In: Runtime, visited tracking, locked-option reasons, interrupt/abort semantics, events, save integration
- Out: Persuasion checks (e22-persuasion-checks)
- Out: UI (e22-dialogue-ui)
- Out: World hookup (e22-npc-conversation)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a dialogue with entries [firstMeeting (not visited), returning], when started twice with the first finished, then the second start uses the `returning` entry.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a choice with a failing condition and `showWhenLocked: true`, when choices are listed, then it appears locked with its describe() reason and cannot be chosen.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a choice whose effect batch fails (e.g. takeItem missing), when chosen, then no effects apply, the runtime routes to the option's `onFail` node if present, else stays on the node with an error event.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a `once` option already chosen, when the dialogue is restarted, then the option is not offered.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a conversation aborted mid-graph, when aborted, then effects already applied remain, no pending effects apply and `dialogue.ended{reason: aborted}` is emitted.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a conversation that sets a fact and gives an item, when saved and reloaded, then fact, item and visited state are preserved.

items.title: Add class- and capability-gated dialogue options with tags
items.description:
## Why
Classes change possibilities — including in conversation (QfG5 class-flavoured solutions; DOS2 tagged options).
## What
As a thief, I want special dialogue options like "[Thief] I couldn't help noticing your ledger doesn't add up" so that my class opens social routes too.

Option `tag` derived from its gating condition: class tag (from class data `dialogueTag`), capability tag (e.g. [Detect Magic]), item tag ([Show the signet ring]). Tags rendered with icons in UI. Designers can mark options hidden-when-locked so other classes don't see them (default hidden for class tags).
## Scope
- In: Tag derivation, default visibility rules, validator warning when a dialogue has class options for < 2 classes (encourages breadth, warning only)
- Out: Persuasion math (e22-persuasion-checks)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an option conditioned on `playerClass: thief`, when listed for a thief, then it is available with tag `thief`; for a knight it is hidden.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an option conditioned on `hasCapability(sense.detect-magic)` with showWhenLocked, when listed without the capability, then it appears locked with tag `sense.detect-magic`.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an option conditioned on `hasItem(signet-ring)`, when listed with the ring, then its tag references the item's icon id.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a dialogue with class-gated options for only one class, when validated, then a warning (not error) is reported.

items.title: Add deterministic persuasion checks with fail branches
items.description:
## Why
DOS2-style persuasion makes talking a real alternative to fighting; failures should create new situations, not reloads.
## What
As a player, I want to persuade, intimidate or deceive characters, with my class, reputation and what I carry affecting the outcome, so that words can solve problems.

`check` node: approach (persuade | intimidate | deceive | charm), difficulty from data, score = disposition-band modifier + class/capability modifiers + item/fact modifiers + NPC personality modifiers. No hidden dice (deterministic, per anti-save-scum and replay determinism); UI can show odds as difficulty labels. Success/failure route to different nodes; failure applies optional effects (disposition drop, alert).
## Scope
- In: Check node evaluation, modifier sources from data, difficulty labels, fail routing
- Out: Haggling specifics (e20-haggling reuses this)
## Notes
Decision: deterministic thresholds (not RNG) so outcomes are learnable and saves do not encourage reroll. Revisit in playtest.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given difficulty 10 and computed score 12, when the check resolves, then the success branch is taken and the breakdown lists each modifier.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same state evaluated twice, when resolved, then the outcome is identical.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a failed intimidate with `onFail: [disposition(-15), emit(alert)]`, when resolved, then both effects apply and the fail node is entered.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a check node without a fail branch, when validated, then validation fails (failures must continue the story).
- AC-5 [unit] Given difficulty labels (easy/fair/hard/impossible), when computed for UI, then they map from score-minus-difficulty per data thresholds.

items.title: Validate dialogues: reachability, exits, references, text limits
items.description:
## Why
Unreachable nodes and dead-ends are invisible bugs; CI must guarantee every conversation can be played through.
## What
Static graph validator over all dialogue content: every node reachable from some entry; every non-end node has at least one exit; every choice node has at least one option available under *some* satisfiable context (not all options contradictory); no infinite loop without an exit option; all item/quest/fact/speaker/capability/dialogue references resolve; text length ≤ configured max per line (UI fit); rumor ids exist. Reports with file + node paths.
## Scope
- In: Validator module, CLI, CI hook, clear error formatting
- Out: Runtime play-testing tool (e22-dialogue-preview-tools)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a dialogue with a node not reachable from any entry, when validated, then validation fails naming the node.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a line node with no `next` and not marked end, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a choice node whose every option requires `playerClass: knight` AND `playerClass: thief`, when validated, then it fails as unsatisfiable.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a cycle A→B→A with no option leaving the cycle, when validated, then it fails with the cycle path.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a line exceeding the max length, when validated, then a warning is produced with the node id and length.
- AC-6 [content] Given all repository dialogue, when CI runs the validator, then it exits 0.

items.title: Start conversations with NPCs in-world and handle interruptions
items.description:
## Why
Conversations must feel embedded in the living world: NPCs stop what they are doing, and danger interrupts talk.
## What
As a player, I want to walk up to an NPC and talk so that conversations flow naturally from exploration.

Interact verb on an NPC with a `dialogueId` starts the runtime; NPC pauses its routine and faces the player; camera shifts to a conversation framing (no cutscene); walking away beyond 6 m or entering combat/alert aborts gracefully; hostile NPCs refuse unless a dialogue entry for hostile state exists (e.g. parley).
## Scope
- In: Interaction binding, NPC routine pause/resume hook, conversation camera framing, abort conditions
- Out: Social creatures (mw-e14 uses this hookup)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an NPC with a dialogue, when the player interacts, then the runtime starts and the NPC's routine state is `conversing`.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a conversation in progress, when a nearby creature enters Alerted/Combat state toward the player, then the conversation aborts within 1 sim tick and the NPC resumes AI control.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player moves more than 6 m away, when detected, then the conversation ends with reason `walked-away`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a hostile NPC with no hostile entry, when interaction is attempted, then no dialogue starts and the prompt says the NPC won't talk.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox NPC, when the player talks, picks two options and ends, then the NPC returns to its patrol route.

items.title: Build accessible dialogue UI with choices, tags and history
items.description:
## Why
Text-only dialogue for MVP means the UI carries all the character; it must be readable and accessible.
## What
As a player, I want clear dialogue text with speaker names, selectable choices and a history log so that I can follow conversations comfortably at my own pace.

Dialogue box: speaker name + portrait slot, text reveal (skippable; speed from settings; instant option), choice list navigable by mouse, number keys and gamepad; class/capability/item tags rendered as icon + label; locked options greyed with reason; persuasion difficulty labels; conversation history (scrollback). Settings hooks: text size, dialogue background opacity, reveal speed, high-contrast.
## Scope
- In: Dialogue screen, input handling, tags, locked reasons, history, settings bindings
- Out: Ambient barks/subtitles (e22-barks-subtitles)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: dialogue box frame, portrait frame, class tag icons ([Knight] [Archer] [Sorcerer] [Thief]), persuasion approach icons (persuade/intimidate/deceive/charm), locked-option icon, generic silhouette portrait placeholder.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given 4 choices, when the player presses the "3" key, then the third choice is selected and confirmed.
- AC-2 [integration] Given reveal speed "instant" in settings, when a line displays, then the full text appears on the first frame.
- AC-3 [integration] Given text size 200%, when a 300-character line and 4 choices display, then all content is visible via wrapping/scroll with no clipping.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a locked option, when focused, then its describe() reason is shown and confirm does nothing.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a finished conversation, when the history panel is opened during a later line, then all previous lines and chosen options are listed in order.
- AC-6 [unit] Given dialogue background opacity 100%, when rendered, then the computed text/background contrast ratio is ≥ 7:1.

items.title: Add rumor system that points players to places and secrets
items.description:
## Why
NPC rumors can lead somewhere (constitution §2); rumors turn conversation into exploration.
## What
As a player, I want NPCs to share rumors that I can follow to real places and secrets so that talking to people leads to discoveries.

Rumor data: `{id, textKey, sources (npc ids / tags like "tavern"), conditions, reveals: {fact, journalEntry, optional mapHint}, resolvesWhen: conditions}`. NPCs draw from rumor pools in dialogue (`revealRumor` effect or a generic "Heard any rumors?" option). Journal "Rumors" section lists heard rumors; a rumor auto-resolves (marked "Investigated") when its target fact is set.
## Scope
- In: Rumor schema + validator, rumor pool selection (deterministic, unheard first), journal integration hook, resolution tracking
- Out: Journal UI rendering (e23-journal-ui)
- Out: Specific rumors (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an NPC with a pool of 3 rumors, 1 already heard, when asked, then an unheard rumor is chosen deterministically (stable order by priority then id).
- AC-2 [unit] Given all pool rumors heard, when asked, then the NPC uses its `noRumors` line and no rumor effect fires.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a heard rumor with `resolvesWhen: fact(well.tunnel.found)`, when that fact is set, then the rumor is marked investigated and a `rumor.resolved` event fires.
- AC-4 [content] Given rumor data, when validated, then every rumor has ≥ 1 source and a resolvesWhen that references an existing fact producer (warning if unproduced).

items.title: Let players give gifts and bribes that shift disposition
items.description:
## Why
Giving the right thing to the right person is a classic QfG-style solution and a gold/item sink.
## What
As a player, I want to offer items or gold to characters, with their tastes deciding the effect, so that knowing people pays off.

NPC `likes`/`dislikes` item tags; a generic "Offer…" dialogue option opens an item picker; effect = disposition delta by taste × value tier; bribes can satisfy dialogue conditions (`bribed` fact). Offering a stolen item to its owner returns it (clears flag) and triggers the owner's `stolenReturned` line.
## Scope
- In: Taste data, offer flow, disposition effect, bribe facts, stolen-return path
- Out: Creature feeding/befriending (mw-e14)

**Integration note:** Promoted to P1 — befriending/helping creatures (Brother Horn, the goblins, Clatter) is an MVP constitution pillar and depends on this.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an NPC who likes `flower` and a flower offered, when resolved, then disposition increases by the liked amount for its value tier.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a disliked item offered, when resolved, then disposition decreases and the item is returned to the player.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stolen item offered to its owner, when resolved, then the item is removed, the stolen flag cleared and the owner's `stolenReturned` node is entered.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a quest item offered to a non-target NPC, when attempted, then the offer is refused and the item stays.

items.title: Show ambient NPC barks as accessible positional subtitles
items.description:
## Why
Overheard lines make the world feel alive and deliver rumors and stealth feedback; without voice they must be readable subtitles.
## What
As a player, I want to read what nearby characters say (guards muttering, merchants calling out) with speaker names and direction so that I overhear the world.

Bark runtime: condition-filtered lines triggered by events (alert state changes, proximity, time), priority + cooldown + anti-repetition. Subtitle display: speaker name, direction indicator for off-screen speakers, max 3 concurrent, respects text size, background opacity and "show speaker names" settings; can be toggled.
## Scope
- In: Bark schema + selector, subtitle HUD, settings hooks
- Out: Merchant bark content (e20-merchant-barks)
- Out: AI state bark triggers wiring (mw-e11 emits events)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: subtitle background plate, off-screen direction chevron.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 5 barks triggered in the same second, when displayed, then at most 3 are visible, ordered by priority.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bark line used once with cooldown 30 s, when triggered again at 10 s, then a different line or no line is chosen.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a speaker behind the camera, when a bark shows, then a direction indicator points toward the speaker.
- AC-4 [integration] Given subtitles disabled for barks in settings, when a bark triggers, then nothing is shown but the bark event is still emitted for telemetry/tests.

items.title: Add dialogue preview runner and debug console commands
items.description:
## Why
Fast content creation (constitution §10): writers need to play a conversation in seconds with any state.
## What
CLI `pnpm dialogue:play <id> --class thief --fact x=true --item y` running the real runtime in the terminal; `pnpm dialogue:graph <id>` exporting Mermaid for docs/review. Debug console: `dlg.start <id>`, `disp.set <npc> <n>`, `fact.set`, `rumor.list`.
## Scope
- In: Terminal runner, Mermaid export, console commands
- Out: A visual dialogue editor (post-MVP)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture dialogue and `--class thief`, when run with scripted choice input, then the transcript matches the snapshot including the thief option.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `dialogue:graph`, when run on a fixture, then the output is valid Mermaid containing every node id.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `disp.set unknown-npc 50`, when executed, then the console reports an unknown NPC and changes nothing.

items.title: Define quest authoring format with objectives and resolutions
items.description:
## Why
Quests must support branching objectives and multiple resolutions without bespoke scripting (E23 outcome).
## What
Quest schema: `id`, `titleKey`, `giverNpcId?`, `startWhen` (conditions) or started by effect, `objectives: [{id, descKey, kind, params, optional?, hidden?, activeWhen}]`, `resolutions: [{id, approach: combat|stealth|diplomacy|magic|trickery|other, when: conditions, effects, journalKey}]`, `failures: [{id, when, effects, continuation: {startQuest | setStage | resolution}}]`, `stages?` for sequencing. All logic via e22-condition-effect-dsl.
## Scope
- In: Schema, 2 fixture quests, format doc section
- Out: Runtime (e23-quest-runtime)
- Out: Validator (e23-quest-validator)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given 2 fixture quests, when validated, then they pass.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a quest with zero resolutions, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a failure without a `continuation`, when validated, then validation fails (failure must continue the story).
- AC-4 [unit] Given an objective with an unknown `kind`, when validated, then validation fails naming it.

items.title: Implement quest state machine with branching and multi-resolution
items.description:
## Why
Quests with several valid resolutions (fight, sneak, talk, trick) are how the game expresses "problems support multiple solutions".
## What
As a designer, I want quests to track objectives and resolve in whichever valid way the player achieves first so that players can solve problems their own way.

States: `unknown → active → resolved(<resolutionId>) | failed(<failureId>)`. Runtime subscribes to world-state/event changes and re-evaluates only affected quests (dependency index on facts/items). Objectives activate/complete per conditions; resolution chosen by first satisfied `when` (priority order for ties). Effects applied atomically; outcome facts written (`quest.<id>.resolution = <id>`). State lives in world-state store (persistent). Emits `quest.*` events for journal/telemetry.
## Scope
- In: State machine, incremental evaluation, objective states, resolution/failure selection, effects, events, persistence
- Out: Objective tracker kinds (e23-objective-trackers)
- Out: Journal (e23-journal-ui)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an active quest with resolutions [slay, persuade], when the persuade conditions become true first, then the quest resolves as `persuade`, its effects apply and `slay` can no longer resolve it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two resolutions satisfied in the same tick, when evaluated, then the one earlier in authored priority wins deterministically.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an optional objective incomplete, when a resolution condition passes, then the quest still resolves and the objective is marked `skipped`.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a resolved quest, when a failure condition later becomes true, then nothing changes (terminal state).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a quest mid-objective, when saved and loaded, then quest state and objective states are identical and evaluation continues.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 50 active quests and 500 fact changes per second in a benchmark, when evaluated, then quest evaluation cost is ≤ 0.5 ms per sim tick on the reference machine.

items.title: Bind quest objective kinds to sim events
items.description:
## Why
Objectives must be satisfiable by any systemic means — a guard removed by sword, sleep spell or trapdoor all count.
## What
As a designer, I want objectives that complete however the player achieves them so that non-combat solutions count automatically.

Objective kinds: `haveItem`, `deliverItem` (to npc), `fact`, `entityState` (dead | befriended | fled | subdued | any-removed — outcome-agnostic so non-combat counts), `enterArea` (trigger volume), `talkTo` / `dialogueNode`, `learnCapability`, `event` (custom emitted event). Each kind registers its event subscriptions and condition translation in the DSL registry.
## Scope
- In: Objective kind implementations, event subscriptions, outcome-agnostic entity removal
- Out: New world events (owned by emitting epics)
## Notes
Encourage designers to use `entityState: removed` rather than `dead` so stealth/diplomacy resolve combat-flavoured objectives.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given objective `entityState(goblin-chief, removed)`, when the chief is killed, befriended into leaving, or flees permanently, then the objective completes in each case.
- AC-2 [unit] Given objective `haveItem(silver-key)`, when the key is acquired then dropped, then the objective completes then reverts to incomplete (unless `latch: true`).
- AC-3 [integration] Given objective `enterArea(mine-entrance)` bound to a trigger volume, when the player enters it, then the objective completes.
- AC-4 [unit] Given objective `deliverItem(ring, mirela)` and the player lacks the ring, when the delivery dialogue option is evaluated, then it is unavailable.

items.title: Make quest failures continue the story instead of dead-ending
items.description:
## Why
Failure creates stories (constitution §2): if the key NPC dies or the thief is caught, the world should adapt.
## What
As a player, I want the story to continue when I fail — a new lead, a harder path, a changed ending — so that I rarely feel the need to reload.

Failure continuation types: start a successor quest, move to an alternate stage, or resolve with a "bittersweet" resolution. Common auto-failure triggers: essential NPC removed, item destroyed, time window elapsed. Runtime guarantees a continuation is applied atomically with the failure. Journal records the failure narratively.
## Scope
- In: Continuation application, built-in failure triggers (npc removed, item destroyed, deadline), journal hook
- Out: Timed world events beyond quest deadlines (mw-e27)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a quest whose giver dies with continuation `startQuest(avenge-giver)`, when the giver is removed, then the original fails and the successor starts in the same tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a quest item destroyed (e.g. burned via e03), when `item.destroyed` fires for it, then the configured failure applies.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a deadline of 3 in-game days, when day 4 begins without resolution, then the failure fires once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a failure continuation referencing a successor that fails to start (conditions false), when applied, then the runtime falls back to the quest's `defaultContinuation` and logs a content error.

items.title: Validate quests are resolvable and failures have continuations
items.description:
## Why
An unresolvable quest is the worst kind of bug; CI must prove every quest can be finished and every failure continues.
## What
Static + symbolic validator: all references resolve (items, npcs, facts, areas, dialogues); every resolution's conditions are satisfiable given the set of known fact/item producers (placements, loot, shops, dialogue effects, other quests); every required item is obtainable somewhere; at least one non-combat resolution exists unless `combatOnly: true` with justification; every failure has a continuation that is itself valid; no quest start depends on its own resolution (cycle).
## Scope
- In: Producer index across content, satisfiability check, cycle detection, CLI + CI hook
- Out: Runtime simulation of full playthroughs (e23-quest-debug-tools)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a resolution requiring item `x` that no placement, loot table, shop or effect produces, when validated, then validation fails naming the quest, resolution and item.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a quest whose only resolution requires `entityState(... dead)` and no `combatOnly` flag, when validated, then a non-combat warning is reported.
- AC-3 [unit] Given quest A starting on B resolved and B starting on A resolved, when validated, then a cycle error is reported.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a fact required by a resolution with no producer, when validated, then validation fails naming the fact.
- AC-5 [content] Given all repository quests, when CI runs the validator, then it exits 0.

items.title: Build in-character journal for quests, rumors and notes
items.description:
## Why
Players need to remember leads and objectives without the game playing itself; an in-character journal keeps the tone.
## What
As a player, I want a journal written in my character's voice listing active, resolved and failed quests, current objectives, heard rumors and notable discoveries so that I can pick up where I left off.

Tabs: Active, Completed/Failed, Rumors, Notes (book excerpts/clues). Entries appended as quest events occur (journalKey per objective/resolution). "New entry" HUD toast. Objectives listed as prose with checkmarks; optional objectives marked. Keyboard/gamepad; text size; pinned quest shown in a compact HUD tracker (toggleable).
## Scope
- In: Journal screen, entry log model (sim) + UI, HUD toast, pinned tracker, settings hooks
- Out: Map/wayfinding markers (e23-wayfinding-hints)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: journal book/parchment frame, tab icons (quest, rumor, note), quest state icons (active, resolved, failed), new-entry toast frame.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a quest started, an objective completed and a rumor heard, when the journal opens, then Active shows the quest with 1 checked objective and Rumors lists the rumor.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a failed quest with a continuation, when viewed, then it appears under Completed/Failed with its failure entry and the successor appears under Active.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a new journal entry, when added, then a toast appears for ≥ 3 s and the journal tab shows an unread indicator until viewed.
- AC-4 [unit] Given text size 150%, when a 10-objective quest is displayed, then content scrolls without clipping.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the pinned tracker is disabled in settings, when a quest is pinned, then no HUD tracker renders.

items.title: Build grey-box reference quest with three resolutions and a failure
items.description:
## Why
An end-to-end fixture proves dialogue, quests, inventory, loot and AI integrate, and gives world-content authors a working template.
## What
As a designer, I want a small grey-box quest demonstrating the full framework so that I can copy it and so CI proves the systems work together.

Testbed-only content (not Briar Glen): an NPC asks the player to recover a stolen item from a guarded room. Resolutions: combat (remove guard), stealth (take item unseen via e18 ownership), diplomacy (persuasion check with the guard), plus a failure (item destroyed → successor quest). Uses a rumor, a class-gated option and a loot container.
## Scope
- In: Fixture content under content/fixtures/, Playwright e2e scripts for each path
- Out: Real game quests (world-content group)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the greybox reference quest, when the combat path is played via scripted input, then the quest resolves as `combat` and the journal shows the resolution entry.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the reference quest, when the stealth path is played (item taken unseen), then it resolves as `stealth` and no crime event was emitted.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the reference quest, when the diplomacy path passes the persuasion check, then it resolves as `diplomacy` without the guard entering Combat state.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the reference quest, when the item is destroyed by fire, then the quest fails and the successor quest becomes active.
- AC-5 [content] Given the fixture, when the quest and dialogue validators run, then both pass.

items.title: Add quest debug commands and "why is this stuck" explainer
items.description:
## Why
Diagnosing stuck quests must be fast for designers and playtest bug reports.
## What
Debug console: `quest.list`, `quest.start <id>`, `quest.objective <id> <obj> complete`, `quest.resolve <id> <res>`, `quest.why <id>` (prints each resolution/objective condition with describe() and current truth values). CLI `pnpm quest:sim <id> --script path` to run a quest against scripted fact/item changes headlessly.
## Scope
- In: Console commands, explainer, headless quest simulator
- Out: Visual quest editor (post-MVP)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an active quest with an unmet resolution condition, when `quest.why` runs, then output lists that condition as false with its describe() text.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `quest.resolve q1 bogus`, when executed, then the console lists valid resolution ids and changes nothing.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a scripted sim of the reference quest stealth path, when run headlessly, then it ends with resolution `stealth`.

items.title: Add optional quest wayfinding hints as an accessibility setting
items.description:
## Why
Default play favours discovery (no waypoints), but some players need help navigating; an opt-in hint respects both.
## What
As a player who gets lost, I want to enable subtle hints toward my pinned objective so that I can keep playing without a guide.

Objectives may author `hintTarget` (entity/area). Setting "Quest hints": Off (default) / Subtle (compass nudge when facing direction) / Clear (on-screen marker). Hints never reveal hidden/secret objectives.
## Scope
- In: Hint target data, three-level setting, compass nudge + marker rendering hook
- Out: Full world map (not planned for MVP)
## Notes
UI assets assumed: compass nudge glyph, objective marker icon.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given setting Off, when a pinned objective has a hintTarget, then no hint renders.
- AC-2 [integration] Given setting Clear, when the target is on-screen, then a marker renders at its projected position; off-screen, an edge arrow renders.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hidden objective with a hintTarget, when any setting is active, then no hint renders for it.

items.title: Write dialogue and quest authoring guide with templates
items.description:
## Why
The world-content group will author Briar Glen NPCs and quests; a clear guide and templates make that fast and consistent.
## What
docs/content/dialogue-and-quests.md: format reference, DSL condition/effect catalogue (generated from the registry), patterns (multiple resolutions, class-gated options, persuasion with fail branches, rumors that lead to places, failure continuations), humour/tone guidance aligned to the tone row in the contract, validator error glossary, copyable templates in content/_templates/.
## Scope
- In: Guide, generated DSL catalogue section, templates for NPC dialogue, merchant, trainer, quest, rumor
- Out: Story bible (e39-story-bible)
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the DSL registry, when the catalogue generator runs, then every registered condition and effect kind appears in the guide section (test compares lists).
- AC-2 [content] Given the templates in content/_templates/, when validated, then each passes its schema.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the guide, when reviewed, then it includes a worked example of a quest with combat, stealth and diplomacy resolutions and a failure continuation.
